advances: An ordinary measurable-subset estimate with a compatible three-fiber realization for convex subsets.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $F(t)=|K\cap H_t|/V$. The subset cap has volume at least $(a-V+VF(t))_+$. Subtracting $\lambda_d a$ from this lower bound gives a function decreasing weakly up to $a=V[1-F(t)]$ and increasing weakly afterwards because $0<\lambda_d\le1$. Its minimum is $-\lambda_d V[1-F(t)]$. The claimed lower bound now follows from the weighted three-tail theorem at $s=-t$, with the two whole-body terms in the same direction and normalized by $V$.

For sharpness in $d\ge2$, use the simplex marginal and equality shift $s_*$ of that theorem. Set $t=-s_*$ and $E=K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\le t\}$. This compact convex cap has $a=V[1-F(-s_*)]>0$ and its intersection with $H_t$ is null. Thus the weighted-tail equality gives equality here. In $d=1$, take a centered interval, $t=0$, and its half on the side opposite $H_0$. Its volume is $V/2$ and the two whole-body caps have total volume $V$. Conversely choosing the measurable complementary cap $E=K\setminus H_t$ in the subset inequality recovers the weighted tail inequality at $s=-t$.

For a convex $E$, a convex combination at an extreme base can only use that same base, so the extreme fibers of the lifted hull are precisely $E$ and $K$. At base zero the hull contains the stated copy of $K$ and lies over $K$ in the continuous coordinates because $E\subset K$ and $K$ is convex. Thus the central fiber is exactly $K$. The affine cap $u\cdot(x-g)\ge -tz$ at the three bases has the required thresholds $t,0,-t$.

For the all-halfspace statement, tighten any containing halfspace until its boundary passes through $(0,g)$. A through-cap with nonzero continuous normal takes the displayed affine form for some $u\ne0$ and $t$. A pure base through-cap contains the whole middle fiber and an entire endpoint, so its mass is at least $V+a\ge\Gamma_d V+\lambda_d a$. Reflection in the base exchanges the endpoints.

statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional convex body of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Let $E\subset K$ be measurable with volume $a$, and let $u\ne0$. Define $H_t=\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge t\}$, $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $\lambda_1=1$ and $\lambda_d=[(2d/(d+1))^{d/(d-1)}-1]^{d-1}$ for $d\ge2$. Then for every real $t$,
$$
|K\cap H_0|+|E\cap H_t|+|K\cap H_{-t}|\ge \Gamma_d V+\lambda_d a.
$$
The coefficient is optimal already for a compact convex $E$. With fibers $E,K,K$ at consecutive bases $-1,0,1$ and measure given by the sum of their Lebesgue volumes, every closed ambient halfspace containing $(0,g)$ has mass at least $\Gamma_d V+\lambda_d a$. The same holds after reversing the endpoint fibers. For convex $E$, these are the exact integer fibers of their lifted convex hull.
title: The sharp weighted payment from a measurable subset and two whole-body caps
